chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Sa'labah, said:

You should say, 'I marry you as Mut'ah upon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), a marriage without adultery, and upon a stipulation that neither will you inherit me nor will I inherit you, for such and such days, with such and such Dirhams, and upon a stipulation that upon you is the waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct verbal formula and set of stipulations for Mut'ah marriage according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the essential verbal formula (sighah) for Mut'ah marriage, explicitly distinguishing it from permanent marriage by stipulating the exclusion of inheritance rights. It underscores the contractual nature of the union by requiring clear specification of duration and dowry, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these elements are integral to the validity of the temporary contract.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Sa’alba,

‘Heasws said: ‘You should be saying, ‘I hereby marry you by Mut’a upon the Book of Allahazwj and a Sunnah of Hisazwj Prophetsaww, a marriage without adultery, and upon a stipulation that neither will you inherit me nor will I inherit you, for such and such days, and with such and such Dirhams, and upon a stipulation that upon you is the waiting period’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Nasr from Tha’labah who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

say, ‘I marry you in the manner of al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) according to the book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Holy prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, a marriage which is not indecency and that you will not inherit me and I will not inherit you, for so and so amount of dirham as mahr (dower) and that you must complete the waiting period.’”
